Round 210 passes: SABA-B-5 part 1 (fast drag of the track, group and Master Volume faders and Pan) is met, with `browserVerified` and `realVerified` both true. I checked everything in a real Chromium browser with real mouse and keyboard, and ran the perf harness twice myself. App source was not touched: the frozen-file hash check and my own tree fingerprint are identical at start and end.

| What I checked | Result |
|---|---|
| Scope | The only gesture-guard change is the one-hunk D-29z183 fix. The other test edits all match A's round-209 table. Exactly the 48 intended budget rows changed. |
| Perf harness ×2 | Both exit 0 with every assert passing, including the 48 rows switched to hard limits. Deterministic results identical between runs; 0 audio restarts during drags. |
| Re-renders per mouse move (production build, 1440×900 and 1280×720) | 1 component per move on all four faders. The old build (`f535ab3`) gives 83 / 85 / 80 / 4 in the same probe. My numbers match the harness exactly. Drags that start below max give 101–104 updates; Pan follows every value change. |
| Live display and audio | The value, readout, fill and live gain agree at every sample. Nothing snaps back after release. One undo entry per drag, and Ctrl+Z restores the gain. |
| Pressing Space mid-drag | The rebuilt audio graph uses the dragged level (−4.8 dB), not the saved one (−12 dB). |
| Loop wrap mid-drag | 6 wraps per drag with no jump back to the saved level. A browser wrap only restarts the sounds; the "graph rebuilt at the wrap" path is covered by the Space check and A's unit test FP8. |
| Group cancel and blur | Cancelling or blurring a group drag puts both member tracks and the display back, with no undo entry. |
| Old build vs new build | 771 behaviour values (keyboard steps, held keys, Shift fine drag, Esc, cancel/blur incl. Pan, double-click reset, undo/redo labels, Pan reset button): 0 differences. 1,062 style values: 0 differences. 32 fader screenshots: pixel-identical. |
| Export | A mix set by dragging and the same mix set by keyboard give bit-identical WAVs (48 kHz, 24-bit, 101.352 s, peak level as expected). The old build gives the same hash. |
| Premium auth | Not bypassed: `/studio-lab` opens anonymously, `/studio/middle-east` asks to sign in, and the Studio token endpoint returns 401 with no header and 500 with a fake Bearer. No token is ever issued. |

Limits B should know about:
- **Pan stolen-claim case (D-29z186):** I couldn't reach it with real input, since a single mouse can't take over a held drag. I re-ran A's test for it (FP13) in a scratch copy: it is green, and removing the guard at `ArrangementContext.tsx` l.2799 turns it red.
- **Single-viewport rows:** the export and the stolen-claim attempt ran at 1440 only; neither depends on viewport size.
- **Screenshots:** the mid-drag screenshot is kept only at 50 %; the other samples are data.
- **Auth script:** my first run of the auth check crashed inside my own script; an identical retry ran clean.

One finding for B:
- **C-R210-01 (Low, docs):** doc 163 lines 68, 69 and 71 still describe the switched budget rows as "record only" and say one harness row will be replaced. Those lines were outside A's grant, and A flagged them. They should go to the deferred polish list or get a one-line grant.

Clean-up: the old-build copy, the scratch copy and the six WAVs (169 MB) are deleted. The WAV hashes are kept.

Files are in `/home/runner/czaba-project/tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- `c-round-210.md` — the full report
- `c-round-210.json`
- `c-browse.json`
- `c-round-210/` — tools, measurements and screenshots
